heroHeadline: 23 Days to Kickoff — Ronaldo Confirmed for Record Sixth World Cup; Scotland Returns After 28 Years; Zurich Summit Today (May 20)
heroSubtitle: Roberto Martínez confirmed Cristiano Ronaldo (41) in Portugal's 26-man World Cup squad on May 19 — Ronaldo becomes the first player in history to compete at six FIFA World Cups. Martínez added a 27th honorary place dedicated to the late Diogo Jota as a tribute from the squad. Key inclusions: Bruno Fernandes, Bernardo Silva, João Neves, Vitinha, Rafael Leão, Gonçalo Ramos, Rúben Dias, Nuno Mendes, Pedro Neto. Portugal face Group K opponents DR Congo, Colombia, and Uzbekistan. Simultaneously, Scotland manager Steve Clarke named his 26-man squad for the nation's first World Cup since France 1998 — a 28-year absence — with captain Andy Robertson (92 caps, Liverpool), Scott McTominay (Napoli), John McGinn (Aston Villa), and Ché Adams (Torino); Scotland open Group C vs Haiti on June 14 at Gillette Stadium, Foxborough. The global squad announcement wave continues: Germany (Nagelsmann, May 21), England (Tuchel, Wembley, May 22 — Ben White out MCL), Spain (De La Fuente, May 25 — Lamine Yamal doubtful with hamstring injury), and USMNT (Pochettino, live NYC event on FOX, May 26 — Pulisic, McKennie, Adams, Balogun expected) still to announce. The Iran/FIFA visa crisis enters its most critical moment: the formal Infantino-Taj Zurich summit takes place today (May 20) — the last diplomatic channel before the June 1 squad deadline; not a single US visa has been issued to any Iranian player or coaching staff member, with Iran training in Antalya, Turkey; warm-up friendly vs Gambia (Antalya, May 29). FIFA submission deadline: June 1; full 48-squad publication: June 2. Tubi/FOX World Cup Hub live with 24/7 programming.
